reason: Both CIFs parse and primitive-standardize as distinct fully occupied 16-atom P-43m (No. 215) In4CuAg3Te8 realizations with a = 8.99556035 A and Z = 1, and the trace provides strong 51-line cubic indexing plus an instantiated integrated-intensity fit (about 6.2% residual); the two submitted models cover the weak 3c/3d In/Ag ordering ambiguity. However, both share a demonstrably untenable periodic framework: all three Ag and three of four In sites have no Te contact shorter than 3.676-3.680 A (their next contacts are still longer), while every Te has only one normally bonded cation neighbor and a 2.659 A Te partner; bond-valence assignment fails. An independent whole-profile check also leaves material atomic-model residual above a Pawley-like bound (unweighted Rwp about 5.93% versus 4.03%). Thus the good metric and intensity match cannot rescue the pervasive underbonding, and another attempt is warranted to instantiate and test a materially different, likely lower-symmetry and/or higher-Z realization rather than the same P-43m framework.
